id: d-001
genre: decisions
title: "Ledgerline stores its data in SQLite"
created: 2026-02-18
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [ledgerline, storage]
status: accepted
related:
  - type: influenced_by
    to: references/sqlite-wal-notes.md
  - type: mentions

---

Context: Ledgerline needs a datastore for timesheets, invoices, and client
records. Studio write volume is small — one billing run a month plus daily
timesheets.

Options considered: Postgres (operational weight, a server to babysit)
versus SQLite (single file, WAL mode, embedded).

Decision: use SQLite in WAL mode as the sole datastore for Ledgerline v1;
Postgres stays out of scope until a second-writer need appears.

Consequences: zero server operations; backups are file copies; the
single-writer ceiling is accepted. Informed by the WAL-mode reading notes
(sqlite-wal-notes).

id: d-002
genre: decisions
title: "Wayfare displays speak MQTT"
created: 2026-02-25
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [wayfare, messaging]
status: accepted
related:
  - type: influenced_by
    to: references/mqtt-311-notes.md
  - type: mentions
    to: projects/wayfare.md
---

Context: platform displays need live vehicle positions with sub-second
perceived freshness; HTTP polling burns battery and lags.

Options considered: HTTP polling against a feed API; MQTT with retained
messages and QoS 1.

Decision: the Wayfare display fleet speaks MQTT 3.1.1 to a transit-side
broker; retained messages let a display recover its last-known state after
reconnect. Informed by mqtt-311-notes.

Consequences: one broker to operate at Halcyon; occasional QoS-1 duplicate
renders, accepted for freshness.

Wayfare is Meridian Studio's realtime departure-display program for Halcyon
Transit: platform displays for three pilot stations — Ashport Central, Ferry
Quay, Millbrook Bridge — fed by live vehicle-position data.

Scope agreed at the kickoff (2026-02-20) with Petra Lindqvist: sub-second
perceived freshness, outdoor readability, and a June ship date. The displays
speak MQTT (decision d-002) and went from per-display autonomy (d-003) to an
edge-gateway hub (d-008) after field maintenance pain. The palette is
green-and-amber for outdoor readability (d-009).

Team: Dev Okonkwo (firmware), Noor Haddad (renderer), June Park (design),
Bram Oyelaran (fleet), Katrin Ilic (QA), Theo Kanda (systems).
Shipped 2026-06-12; ship retro in m-008.

id: d-003
genre: decisions
title: "Wayfare runs one single-board computer per display, no central server"
created: 2026-03-04
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [wayfare, architecture]
status: superseded
related:
  - type: influenced_by
    to: references/embedded-single-board-notes.md
  - type: mentions
    to: projects/wayfare.md
---

Context: each platform display needs local rendering; per-display autonomy
avoids putting a central server in stations.

Options considered: per-display autonomy with single-board computers; a
station hub coordinating its displays.

Decision: each Wayfare display runs its own single-board computer with local
fallback rendering and no central station server — autonomy per display,
informed by the single-board field notes (embedded-single-board-notes).

Consequences: wiring stays simple; firmware updates must be flashed board by
board. Superseded by d-008 after field maintenance pain (s-004, m-005).

id: d-008
genre: decisions
title: "Wayfare moves to an edge-gateway hub per station"
created: 2026-04-08
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [wayfare, architecture]
status: accepted
related:

    to: decisions/d-003.md
  - type: influenced_by

  - type: influenced_by

  - type: mentions

---

Context: after six weeks in the field, per-display autonomy shows its cost —
firmware drift across boards and roughly ninety minutes of manual reflash per
display when updates land (documented in s-004, reviewed in m-005).

Options considered: keep per-display autonomy with a better flashing ritual;
one edge gateway per station coordinating its displays.

Decision: each pilot station gets an edge gateway hub — firmware flashes once
per station, displays pull from the gateway, telemetry funnels through it.
This supersedes d-003.

Consequences: one more box per station, collapsed maintenance surface; Bram
owns gateway provisioning.

Retro after shipping Wayfare on 2026-06-12. What worked: the edge-gateway
reversal (d-008) collapsed the maintenance surface — flashing is now a
station visit, not a fleet archaeology dig; Odessa's platform contrast
testing made the green-and-amber palette readable in full sun; MQTT retained
messages recovered cleanly through network drops. What hurt: QoS 1 delivered
duplicate renders during reconnects — next time, dedupe on the display, not
in ops. Katrin's QA signoff checklist is adopted as the studio default for
client ships.

Context: Ashport Central's platform is sunlit most of the day; the first
palette washed out in daylight.

Options considered: the original blue-on-dark palette; green-and-amber after
Odessa's contrast testing at the platform (s-008) and the WCAG contrast
notes.

Decision: Wayfare's displays render in green-and-amber — green for live
departures, amber for alerts and delays — both testing well above the
contrast floor in daylight.

Consequences: renderer theming is a config swap; June owns the design tokens.

final_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, **Dev Okonkwo built Wayfare's display firmware** and **Noor Haddad built the Wayfare display renderer**.

**Dev Okonkwo (firmware):**
- He "owns the Wayfare display firmware" and "brought up the first Wayfare display on the bench" (people/dev-okonkwo.md)
- He worked on the architecture decisions for per-display autonomy (d-003) and the later edge-gateway hub migration (d-008) after field maintenance pain surfaced during an April field day (people/dev-okonkwo.md)

**Noor Haddad (renderer):**
- She "built the Wayfare display renderer" (people/noor-haddad.md)
- She joined "Wayfare's final stretch" after Beacon Grid paused in late May (people/noor-haddad.md)
- The renderer adopted the green-and-amber palette for outdoor readability (d-009), with theming as a config swap

The project page confirms: "Team: Dev Okonkwo (firmware), Noor Haddad (renderer)..." (projects/wayfare.md)
